# Stage 1 build, round 2 — contract for the fix run (2026-10-04)

Authority: Sean Borycki, program lead, wrote in the session on 2026-10-04: "G0 set to Approved in both trackers; proceed with builder fixes." (The live plan's G0 dropdown still read "Awaiting approval" at rev 12 when checked immediately after; register R-043 stays open until a tracker shows Approved.)

Baseline: this working copy is the delivered package (vcr-stage1-build.zip) committed as d6306f3 in a fresh git repository. Every fix is made here. The reviewer's package copy (scratchpad/vcr) and the research bundle (scratchpad/inputs) are read-only references.

Findings register: scratchpad/pm/issues_register.csv (77 rows; ids R-001…R-077). Reviewer reports: scratchpad/pm/reviewer_report_G1-prep_2026-10-04.md, …_pass2_…, builder_items_adjudication.md. A fix closes a register row only if it meets the row's description and reference; partial fixes are reported as partial.

## Scope of this round

Builder-owned rows only. Rows owned by Sean, the SME or the statistician are NOT pre-empted; they are listed in OPEN_DECISIONS.md (head agent writes it) and the files they govern are left as they are:
R-004 (closed by git init), R-021, R-023, R-025, R-027, R-029, R-032, R-033, R-034, R-038 (environment route — scripts must nevertheless run under both renv and a system library), R-041, R-043, R-044 (appraisal item lists), R-045 (dual rating / adjudicator), R-046, R-047, R-048, R-049, R-050, R-056, R-058, R-059, R-060, R-061, R-062, R-063, R-065, R-066, R-071 (blind-first SME rating), R-074.
Exception, R-068: the screening DRAFT criterion that excludes validated self-report outcomes contradicts charter decision 2 (pain and seizure frequency are named health outcomes) and the research document's scope ("measured objectively or by a validated rating"). It is aligned to the charter in this round and marked "confirm at G2".

## Cross-cutting decisions (binding on every fixer)

1. master_extraction.csv gains two columns, already added to the header in this copy, after `n_tested`: `pre_post_r` (correlation between pre and post measurements for within-person designs, as printed or derivable; blank if not reported) and `is_primary_outcome` (`yes`/`no`; exactly one `yes` per study × ability; set by the head agent at reconciliation, not by extractors). SCHEMA.md documents both (fixer C).
2. Effect sizes are computed by analysis code from the master file (SCHEMA convention), never hand-built. New script analysis/01_effect_sizes.R writes analysis/outputs/effect_sizes.csv with exactly these columns:
   `es_id, study_id, ability_id, outcome_measure, timepoint, design, lever_type, measure, yi, vi, n_i, n_c, is_primary_outcome, synthetic, derivation`
   `measure` ∈ {SMD (independent groups: rct, nonrandomised_comparison), SMCR (within-person: pre_post, crossover; uses pre_post_r or the placeholder), PLO (prevalence: logit proportion from n_responders/n_tested), OR (log odds ratio from two binary rows), Z (Δ/σ_pop with delta-method variance, only where a `verified` population_sd row exists)}. `synthetic` is `yes` when study_id starts with `synth_`.
   SE→SD: sd = se·√n. CI95→SD: sd = (hi−lo)/(2·1.96)·√n. Recorded in `derivation`.
3. Placeholder pre/post correlation: when `pre_post_r` is blank for an SMCR row, r = 0.5 is used, with sensitivity runs at 0.3 and 0.7. Declared once in analysis/constants.R as `R_PREPOST_DEFAULT`, labelled "placeholder pending the statistician co-author's decision at Gate 5" everywhere it is mentioned.
4. Pooling unit: ability_id × measure, using rows with `is_primary_outcome = yes` only; non-primary rows are reported individually. (Dependent effect sizes: multilevel alternative is a Gate 5 decision; say so in a comment.)
5. freq_pooled.csv always has the columns `ability_id, measure, outcome_measure, k, est, ci_lb, ci_ub, pi_lb, pi_ub, tau2, I2, p, note` (NA where not pooled). freq_individual.csv has `es_id, study_id, ability_id, measure, outcome_measure, yi, ci_lb, ci_ub, k_ability` for every row (ci = yi ± 1.96·√vi; back-transformed for PLO in extra columns `est_natural, ci_lb_natural, ci_ub_natural`). bayes_pooled.csv has `ability_id, measure, k, mu_mean, mu_lb, mu_ub, tau_median, p_mu_gt_0.2, p_mu_gt_0.5, pred_lb, pred_ub, bf_10, mu_mean_wider, mu_mean_tighter, note`; only SMD/SMCR/Z measures run through the declared SMD-scale priors; PLO/OR rows get a note row ("Beta-binomial / logit model: Gate 5"). Every bayesmeta call is wrapped in tryCatch and the error goes to `note`; the script must not halt when bayesmeta is absent — it writes note rows and a warning.
6. grade_draft.csv header: `ability_id, outcome, n_studies, n_participants, design_mix, starting_level, rob_downgrade, inconsistency_downgrade, indirectness_downgrade, imprecision_downgrade, publication_bias_downgrade, large_effect_upgrade, dose_response_upgrade, opposing_confounding_upgrade, draft_certainty, reasons, plain_language_statement, rater_id, date, skill_version, model`. grade_final.csv = the same columns plus `final_certainty, final_rater_id, final_date, change_reason, signed`. `outcome` equals the primary row's `outcome_measure` string, so 03_sof.R joins on `ability_id` + `outcome`.
7. Screening: a review, meta-analysis or overview is `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7`; the word `harvest` is no longer a code value (SCHEMA and skill agree). E7 is tested first, then E1…E5, E8. E6 (duplicate) is applied by the head agent during deduplication, never by a screener.
8. Trace format stays as implemented (`s<N>-<role>-<instance>-<ts>-<hex>`, `traces/stage<N>.jsonl`); TRACE_SPEC.md is corrected to match. The logger serialises writes with a lock file and atomic replace; `end` adds `--tool-calls` (JSON), `--safety-stop-subject`, `--transcript PATH` (copied to traces/transcripts/<trace_id>.<ext>, sha recorded, `transcript_kind` ∈ {platform_export, final_report_only, none}); `selection_policy` is validated against `single_run | first_completed | best_of_n:<criterion>`; both subcommands take `--started-at/--ended-at` overrides and `--retroactive` (sets `retroactive: true`) for records written after the fact.
9. No fixer edits README.md, CHANGELOG.md, OPEN_DECISIONS.md or BUILD_CONTRACT.md, and no fixer commits. Each fixer writes `CHANGELOG_<area>.md` at the package root: one line per register id — `R-0xx | files changed | what changed | how verified (command and result)` — plus a "Not closed" list with reasons.
10. Environment here: R 4.3.3 with metafor 4.4.0, dplyr, readr, digest, jsonlite, ggplot2, renv (system library, apt); bayesmeta and meta are NOT installed and cannot be (CRAN blocked); Python 3 standard library; no network to publishers or standards hosts. Every script must run end to end in this environment on synthetic data; what cannot run (bayesmeta) must degrade to note rows, not errors.
11. Standing conditions: nothing is submitted, registered, contacted, spent, published or scheduled. No connectors (Gmail, Drive, GitHub), no scheduled tasks, no web posting. Do not touch /home/user/chick-contact-system.

content.content:
1	# Schema dictionary
     2	
     3	All CSV files in this package are UTF-8, comma-separated, header row as given, blank cell = missing. This file defines seven of them: master_extraction.csv, screening_decisions.csv, appraisal.csv, population_sd.csv, grade_draft.csv, grade_final.csv (header templates in schema/; live files are written where each section says) and the reconciliation files (discrepancies.csv, adjudication_log.csv, master_reconciled.csv; layout here, procedure in tools/RECONCILIATION.md). The analysis code (analysis/00_load.R) refuses any master row whose provenance fields (source_doi or source_url, location, verbatim_anchor, extractor_id, extraction_date, verification_route) are empty, whose skill_version or model is blank, or whose controlled-vocabulary values are outside the lists below.
     4	
     5	## master_extraction.csv — one row per outcome × condition × timepoint
     6	Header template: schema/master_extraction.csv. Extractor files are written to extraction/<study or batch>_A.csv and _B.csv; the analysis reads only extraction/master_reconciled.csv (see Reconciliation).
     7	
     8	| Field | Meaning / allowed values |
     9	|---|---|
    10	| study_id | `firstauthor_year` plus a letter if needed (`benson_1982a`); `synth_` prefix marks synthetic test data |
    11	| record_id | id from the records file |
    12	| ability_id | A01–A26 (skills/screening/references/abilities.md); semicolon-separated if a row informs more than one |
    13	| design | `rct`, `crossover`, `nonrandomised_comparison`, `pre_post`, `case_report`, `case_series`, `prevalence_survey`, `other` (state in notes) |
    14	| population | free text as printed (age, health status, expertise) |
    15	| n_total | total analysed in the study |
    16	| condition_label | `intervention`, `control`, `baseline`, `sham`, or the printed label; never blank |
    17	| n_condition | n analysed in this condition (needed for every SE or CI conversion) |
    18	| comparator_label | `condition_label` of the row this one is compared with, blank if none; the code pairs rows on study_id + outcome_measure + timepoint + this label |
    19	| lever_type | `feedback`, `breathing`, `muscle`, `imagery`, `suggestion`, `none`, `mixed`, `unclear` |
    20	| outcome_measure | what was measured, as printed (`hearing threshold at 250 Hz`); the same string on every row of that outcome, because it is a key field |
    21	| instrument | device or method (`tympanometry`, `infrared thermistor`) |
    22	| unit | as printed |
    23	| timepoint | as printed (`end of 12 weeks`, `during contraction`) |
    24	| stat_type | `mean`, `median`, `mean_change`, `percent`, `count`, `max_individual`, `other` |
    25	| value | the number as printed |
    26	| dispersion_type | `SD`, `SE`, `CI95`, `IQR`, `range`, `none` |
    27	| dispersion_value | SD, SE or IQR width as printed, never converted; for CI95 use ci_low and ci_high and leave this blank |
    28	| ci_low, ci_high | as printed |
    29	| p_value | as printed (`<0.001`, `0.03`) |
    30	| baseline_value, baseline_dispersion | pre-intervention values on the same row when the paper reports change from baseline (within-person designs) |
    31	| n_responders, n_tested | prevalence designs and binary outcomes: numerator and denominator |
    32	| pre_post_r | within-person designs (`pre_post`, `crossover`): correlation between the pre and post measurements, as printed or derivable from printed numbers (derivation stated); numeric in [−1, 1]; blank if not reported. Blank rows get the placeholder r = 0.5 in analysis (see Effect-size conventions). Recorded by extractors, never estimated |
    33	| is_primary_outcome | `yes`/`no`; exactly one primary outcome (one `outcome_measure` string, all its rows flagged `yes`) per study × ability. Extractors leave it blank; the head agent sets it at reconciliation from the primary-outcome file (`tools/reconcile.py build --primary`), following the pre-specified outcome hierarchy agreed for the protocol. Only `yes` rows enter pooling |
    34	| value_source | `text`, `table`, `figure`, `supplement`, `derived` |
    35	| derivation | formula and inputs if `derived` (also for a derived pre_post_r) |
    36	| source_doi, source_url | at least one required |
    37	| location | page, table, figure or section (`p. 1236, Table 2, row 3`) |
    38	| verbatim_anchor | ≤ 20 words copied exactly from the location |
    39	| extractor_id | `agent-extraction-A`, `agent-extraction-B`, `human-<initials>`; `reconciled` in master_reconciled.csv (written by tools/reconcile.py) |
    40	| extraction_date | ISO date |
    41	| verification_route | `pdf_full_text`, `html_full_text`, `supplement`, `abstract_only`, `not_opened` (the last two are provisional and stop the analysis) |
    42	| skill_version | git short hash of skills/extraction at run time; in master_reconciled.csv `A=<hash>;B=<hash>` when the two runs differ |
    43	| model | exact model string from the run; in master_reconciled.csv `A=<string>;B=<string>` when the two runs differ |
    44	| notes | free text; reasons for blanks |
    45	
    46	Key fields: `study_id`, `ability_id`, `outcome_measure`, `condition_label`, `timepoint` identify a row and must be unique within one extractor file; the reconciliation diff matches rows on them.
    47	
    48	## screening_decisions.csv
    49	Header template: schema/screening_decisions.csv; live file screening/screening_decisions.csv.
    50	record_id · stage (`ta`, `ft`) · decision (`include`, `exclude`, `unsure`) · exclusion_code (`E1`, `E2`, `E3`, `E4`, `E5`, `E6`, `E7`, `E8` or blank; no other value) · rationale (≤ 40 words with a quoted phrase) · confidence (`high`, `medium`, `low`) · screener_id (`agent-screening-A`, `agent-screening-B`, `human-<initials>`, `head-agent` for E6 only) · skill_version · model · timestamp (ISO 8601).
    51	
    52	Coding conventions (skills/screening/SKILL.md):
    53	- A review, meta-analysis or overview is `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7`. There is no `harvest` code value; reference-list mining of E7 records is a Stage 3 head-agent step. PRISMA flow: E7 records count as excluded at the stage where they were coded, and the mined references enter the flow as "records identified from citation searching".
    54	- Codes are tested in the order E7, E1, E2, E3, E4, E5; E8 (full text not obtainable) always pairs with `decision = unsure`.
    55	- E6 (duplicate) is written only by the head agent during deduplication (`screener_id = head-agent`); screener rows never carry it.
    56	- Agreement statistics (κ) are computed on `decision` and, among excludes, on `exclusion_code`.
    57	
    58	## appraisal.csv
    59	Header template: schema/appraisal.csv; live file appraisal/appraisal.csv.
    60	study_id · tool (`rob2`, `rob2_crossover`, `robins_i`, `jbi_case_report`, `jbi_case_series`, `jbi_prevalence`) · tool_version (date or version string) · domain (tool's domain or item name, or `overall`) · judgment (tool vocabulary; see skills/appraisal/SKILL.md) · rationale · source_location · rater_id (`agent-appraisal`, `agent-appraisal-A`, `agent-appraisal-B`, `human-<initials>`) · date · skill_version · model · notes (tool-selection rule used, and anything else).
    61	
    62	## population_sd.csv
    63	Resting-value sources for the Z scale (schema/population_sd.csv, read directly by 00_load.R).
    64	ability_id (A-codes, semicolon-separated when shared) · variable · mean · sd · unit (matched case-insensitively to the master row's `unit`) · population · n (persons; blank when the source counts measurements or eyes, stated in notes) · source_doi · source_citation · location · status (`pilot_unverified` until a dual-extracted row with provenance replaces it; `verified` thereafter) · notes (sample descriptors from the research document, URL when there is no DOI, derivation notes).
    65	The analysis code uses only `verified` rows; every row shipped in this package is `pilot_unverified`, so no Z effect size is computed until re-extraction (charter SC1).
    66	
    67	## grade_draft.csv
    68	Header template: schema/grade_draft.csv (21 columns, in this order); live file reporting/grade_draft.csv, one row per ability × primary outcome, written by the appraisal skill.
    69	
    70	| Field | Meaning / allowed values |
    71	|---|---|
    72	| ability_id | A01–A26 |
    73	| outcome | the primary row's `outcome_measure` string, copied exactly, so that 04_sof.R can join on ability_id + outcome |
    74	| n_studies | number of studies contributing to this ability × outcome (k of the pooled unit, or 1) |
    75	| n_participants | sum of analysed participants across those studies |
    76	| design_mix | semicolon-separated design counts (`rct:2;pre_post:3`) |
    77	| starting_level | `High`, `Low`, `Very low` (rule in skills/appraisal/SKILL.md) |
    78	| rob_downgrade, inconsistency_downgrade, indirectness_downgrade, imprecision_downgrade, publication_bias_downgrade | `0`, `-1` or `-2` |
    79	| large_effect_upgrade, dose_response_upgrade, opposing_confounding_upgrade | `0`, `1` or `2`; non-zero only for non-randomised evidence without serious risk of bias |
    80	| draft_certainty | `High`, `Moderate`, `Low`, `Very low`: the arithmetic result of starting level plus downgrades and upgrades |
    81	| reasons | one sentence per non-zero domain naming the studies driving it, separated by `;` |
    82	| plain_language_statement | GRADE informative statement for the Summary of Findings |
    83	| rater_id | `agent-appraisal` (or `-A`/`-B`) |
    84	| date | ISO date |
    85	| skill_version | git short hash of skills/appraisal at run time |
    86	| model | exact model string from the run |
    87	
    88	## grade_final.csv
    89	Header template: schema/grade_final.csv = the 21 grade_draft.csv columns in the same order plus five; live file reporting/grade_final.csv, written by the subject-matter co-author from the draft (one row per draft row; the draft columns are copied, not edited, so the pair (draft_certainty, final_certainty) gives the GRADE concordance output, reporting/METHODS_PAPER_OUTCOMES.md #6). 04_sof.R reads ability_id, outcome, n_studies, n_participants, final_certainty, reasons, plain_language_statement and joins on ability_id + outcome.
    90	
    91	| Field | Meaning / allowed values |
    92	|---|---|
    93	| final_certainty | `High`, `Moderate`, `Low`, `Very low`: the co-author's rating |
    94	| final_rater_id | `human-<initials>` of the subject-matter co-author |
    95	| final_date | ISO date of the final rating |
    96	| change_reason | why final differs from draft; blank when they agree |
    97	| signed | `yes` once the co-author has signed the table for the Summary of Findings, else `no`; 04_sof.R reports unsigned rows |
    98	
    99	## Reconciliation files (tools/reconcile.py; procedure in tools/RECONCILIATION.md)
   100	- discrepancies.csv (`reconcile.py diff`): discrepancy_id (`D-0001`…, deterministic for a given pair of input files) · key (the five key fields joined with `|`) · field (a master column, or `row` when the whole row is in one file only) · value_A · value_B · type (`missing_in_A`, `missing_in_B`, `numeric`, `text`, `provenance`).
   101	- adjudication_log.csv (Sean): discrepancy_id · decision (`A`, `B`, `other`) · chosen_value (required for `other`) · adjudicator · date (ISO) · reason. Every discrepancy needs one row; `build` refuses otherwise.
   102	- master_reconciled.csv (`reconcile.py build`): the master_extraction.csv columns, extractor_id `reconciled`, extraction_date = build date, skill_version and model merged as above, is_primary_outcome set from the primary-outcome file (study_id, ability_id, outcome_measure) or left blank with a warning. Read by analysis/00_load.R as extraction/master_reconciled.csv.
   103	
   104	## Effect-size conventions (computed in analysis code, never by extractors)
   105	analysis/01_effect_sizes.R reads master_reconciled.csv and writes analysis/outputs/effect_sizes.csv with the columns `es_id, study_id, ability_id, outcome_measure, timepoint, design, lever_type, measure, yi, vi, n_i, n_c, is_primary_outcome, synthetic, derivation`. `measure` is one of:
   106	- `SMD` — independent groups (`rct`, `nonrandomised_comparison`): Hedges' g with small-sample correction from means, SDs and n per condition (metafor `escalc(measure = "SMD")`).
   107	- `SMCR` — within-person designs (`pre_post`, `crossover`): standardised mean change using the raw-score (pre) SD, with the pre/post correlation taken from `pre_post_r`. When `pre_post_r` is blank, the placeholder r = 0.5 is used (analysis/constants.R `R_PREPOST_DEFAULT`, placeholder pending the statistician co-author's decision at Gate 5) with sensitivity runs at r = 0.3 and 0.7.
   108	- `PLO` — prevalence designs: logit-transformed proportion from `n_responders`/`n_tested`; back-transformed to a proportion for reporting.
   109	- `OR` — binary outcomes compared across two rows: log odds ratio from the two `n_responders`/`n_tested` pairs.
   110	- `Z` — Δ/σ_pop with delta-method variance Var(z) ≈ Var(Δ)/σ² + Δ²·Var(σ)/σ⁴, Var(σ) ≈ σ²/(2(n_pop − 1)); computed only where a `verified` population_sd.csv row matches the ability_id and unit, in addition to SMD/SMCR for the same pair.
   111	- Conversions, recorded in `derivation`: SE → SD, sd = se·√n; CI95 → SD, sd = (hi − lo)/(2·1.96)·√n. No other interval is converted.
   112	- `synthetic` is `yes` when study_id starts with `synth_`; synthetic rows never enter a reported table.
   113	
   114	Pooling unit: ability_id × measure, using rows with `is_primary_outcome = yes` only; non-primary rows are reported individually (freq_individual.csv) and never pooled. Frequentist pooling at k ≥ 3 (charter D1); below that, individual intervals plus the Bayesian posterior. Dependent effect sizes within a pooling unit (several timepoints or conditions of one study) are a known limitation; the multilevel alternative is a Gate 5 decision. Bayesian pooling runs only on SMD/SMCR/Z measures under the declared SMD-scale priors; PLO/OR rows get a note row ("Beta-binomial / logit model: Gate 5").

=== screening SKILL
     1	---
     2	name: vcr-screening
     3	description: Title/abstract and full-text screening for the voluntary-control systematic review, applied as one of two blinded screeners. Use this skill whenever you are asked to screen records, decide inclusion or exclusion, apply eligibility criteria, or produce rows for screening_decisions.csv for this review, even if the request just says "go through these records" or "which of these are in scope".
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Screening skill (one of two blinded screeners)
     7	
     8	You are screener A or screener B. You never read, open or ask about the other screener's decisions. The head agent computes agreement afterwards and routes disagreements to Sean.
     9	
    10	## Inputs
    11	- A records file (CSV) with at least: record_id, title, abstract, year, authors, source_db, doi (may be blank).
    12	- The stage: `ta` (title and abstract) or `ft` (full text). At `ft` you also receive the full-text path for each record.
    13	- The eligibility criteria. Until Gate 2 registers them, use the DRAFT criteria below. After Gate 2, replace the block with the registered text verbatim and bump `skill_version`.
    14	
    15	## Output
    16	One row per record in schema/screening_decisions.csv (see schema/SCHEMA.md). Required fields: record_id, stage, decision, exclusion_code, rationale, confidence, screener_id, skill_version, model, timestamp. Decision values: `include`, `exclude`, `unsure`. Exclusion codes: E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E7, E8 or blank; there is no other code value (E6 is reserved for the head agent, see below).
    17	
    18	## Rules
    19	1. Decide from the record text only. Do not search the web to resolve a record at `ta`; do not open other papers.
    20	2. At `ta`, `unsure` means include for full-text review. At `ft`, `unsure` is allowed only with a rationale stating what is missing; it goes to Sean.
    21	3. Test E7 first: if the record is a review, meta-analysis or overview, write `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7` and stop; do not go on to the other codes (a review has no primary measurement and no extractable primary result of its own, so E3 and E4 would otherwise fire first and hide the review from reference-list mining). Otherwise apply E1 to E5 in numeric order and record the first that applies; E8 applies only when the full text could not be opened (rule 5).
    22	4. The rationale is at most 40 words and must cite a phrase from the record ("abstract: 'participants were instructed to…'"). Do not paraphrase content that is not in the record.
    23	5. If a full text could not be opened, decision = `unsure`, exclusion_code = `E8`, rationale = where you tried. Never decide from a snippet.
    24	6. Reviews, meta-analyses and narrative overviews are `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7`. They are not included and are appraised nowhere. The head agent mines the reference lists of all E7 records at Stage 3 (reference-list mining, formerly called "harvest"; `harvest` is not a code value and must not appear in `decision` or `exclusion_code`).
    25	7. One record per row; multi-report studies are linked later by the head agent, not merged by you. You never judge whether a record duplicates another one.
    26	8. Log the run with traces/trace_logger.py before and after (role `screening`, instance A or B).
    27	
    28	## DRAFT eligibility criteria (pending Gate 2 registration)
    29	- Population: living humans of any age, healthy or clinical.
    30	- Exposure: a deliberate attempt by the person to change a bodily function in references/abilities.md, with or without a lever (feedback, breathing, muscle tension, imagery, suggestion or hypnosis).
    31	- Comparator: any — within-person baseline or rest, sham, control group, or a population norm — or none for prevalence surveys.
    32	- Outcome: an instrumented physiological measurement, or a validated rating instrument for pain (intensity, unpleasantness) or a seizure diary/count; unvalidated self-report alone is not an outcome. For prevalence designs, the proportion of people who can perform the function counts as the outcome. Aligned to charter D2 (pain and seizure frequency are named health outcomes) and the research document's scope ("measured objectively or by a validated rating"); confirm at G2 (R-068).
    33	- Design: any empirical design including case reports and prevalence surveys. Reviews, meta-analyses and overviews are excluded with E7 (their reference lists are mined by the head agent at Stage 3).
    34	- Language and date: any.
    35	
    36	### Exclusion codes, in the order they are tested
    37	- E7 review, meta-analysis or overview → `decision = exclude`, `exclusion_code = E7` (tested first; stop here if it applies)
    38	- E1 non-human or in vitro
    39	- E2 no deliberate attempt by the person (placebo responses, classical conditioning, passive stimulation, drug effects)
    40	- E3 no admissible measurement: neither an instrumented physiological measurement nor a validated rating instrument for pain or a seizure diary/count (unvalidated self-report or observer impression only)
    41	- E4 no extractable quantitative result (no numbers, no figure, no table)
    42	- E5 function not in references/abilities.md and not a reasonable addition (flag additions as `unsure` with the proposed function named)
    43	- E8 full text not obtainable → `decision = unsure`, `exclusion_code = E8`, for Sean
    44	
    45	Head-agent code, never applied by a screener: E6 duplicate publication of a record already screened. Deciding E6 needs knowledge of other records, which rules 1 and 7 forbid you. The head agent applies E6 during deduplication of the records file (before `ta` screening and again when linking multi-report studies) and records it under `screener_id = head-agent`.
    46	
    47	## Human subset
    48	Before `ta` screening starts, the head agent draws a seeded random 10–20% subset of records (seed recorded in the trace). The two human co-authors (the statistician co-author and the subject-matter co-author; charter D4) screen that subset blind, in the same CSV format with `screener_id = human-<initials>`, so that agent-vs-human κ can be computed at Gate 3 (reporting/METHODS_PAPER_OUTCOMES.md #3). Sean adjudicates agent–agent and agent–human disagreements and therefore does not code the subset. You are not told which records are in the subset.

=== RECONCILIATION.md
     1	# Reconciliation of the two extractor files
     2	
     3	How extractor A's and extractor B's rows become `extraction/master_reconciled.csv`, the only file `analysis/00_load.R` reads. Tool: `tools/reconcile.py` (Python 3 standard library, no installs). File layouts are also in `schema/SCHEMA.md` (Reconciliation files).
     4	
     5	## Roles
     6	- Extractors A and B (agents, `skills/extraction/SKILL.md`) each write a complete file in the `schema/master_extraction.csv` layout, blind to each other.
     7	- The head agent runs the diff, hands the discrepancy list to Sean, runs the build, and records every step in the trace (role `head`, inputs = the two extractor files and the log, output = the reconciled file).
     8	- Sean adjudicates every discrepancy in `adjudication_log.csv`. Agents never fill the log.
     9	- The statistician co-author spot-checks the reconciled file (reporting/METHODS_PAPER_OUTCOMES.md #4).
    10	
    11	## Procedure
    12	1. Collect the two files, e.g. `extraction/master_A.csv` and `extraction/master_B.csv`. Both must carry the five key fields `study_id, ability_id, outcome_measure, condition_label, timepoint`, unique per row within a file (the tool refuses duplicates and names the lines).
    13	2. Diff: `python3 tools/reconcile.py diff extraction/master_A.csv extraction/master_B.csv --out extraction/discrepancies.csv`. The tool prints the row counts and the count per discrepancy type. The discrepancy ids (`D-0001`…) are assigned in sorted key order and are stable as long as the two input files do not change; if either file is edited, re-run the diff and re-check the log.
    14	3. Sean fills `extraction/adjudication_log.csv`, one row per discrepancy id (schema below). `decision = A` or `B` takes that extractor's value; `other` takes `chosen_value` (for example the value re-read from the paper when both extractors were wrong). For a whole-row discrepancy (`field = row`) the decision is `A` or `B` only: choosing the file in which the row is present keeps it, choosing the other file drops it.
    15	4. Build: `python3 tools/reconcile.py build extraction/master_A.csv extraction/master_B.csv extraction/adjudication_log.csv --primary extraction/primary_outcomes.csv --out extraction/master_reconciled.csv [--date YYYY-MM-DD]`. The tool recomputes the discrepancies, checks the log, and refuses to write anything (exit 2) while any discrepancy lacks a log row, while the log names an id that is not a discrepancy of these files, or while a log row is malformed. Each problem is one line on stderr.
    16	5. Keep A, B, discrepancies.csv, adjudication_log.csv and primary_outcomes.csv next to master_reconciled.csv; they are part of the Gate 7 release and the methods-paper source for outcome #4 (field-level exact-agreement rate = 1 − discrepancies / compared cells; numeric discrepancy rate = `numeric` rows / compared numeric cells; discrepancies by type from the `type` column, with Sean's `reason` giving the misread/wrong-row/unit/omission category).
    17	6. Run `Rscript analysis/00_load.R` (or `run_all.R`) from the package root. The loader refuses rows with blank provenance, out-of-vocabulary values or provisional verification routes, and warns for any study × ability without an `is_primary_outcome = yes` row.
    18	
    19	## What is compared
    20	- All master columns except the key fields and the run-metadata fields. Values are compared after trimming whitespace. Two numeric strings that are numerically equal (`1` and `1.0`) are not a discrepancy; the reconciled file keeps A's printed form.
    21	- Types: `missing_in_A` / `missing_in_B` (one extractor has a value, the other a blank; or, with `field = row`, the whole row exists in one file only), `numeric` (both numeric and different), `text` (any other difference), `provenance` (any difference in source_doi, source_url, location, verbatim_anchor or verification_route, whatever its form, so that provenance conflicts are adjudicated as such and never auto-merged).
    22	- Not compared: `extractor_id`, `extraction_date`, `skill_version`, `model`. They describe the run, not the paper, and always differ between A and B. In the reconciled file `extractor_id = reconciled`, `extraction_date` = the build date, and `skill_version` / `model` are the common value or `A=<a>;B=<b>`.
    23	
    24	## adjudication_log.csv
    25	| Column | Content |
    26	|---|---|
    27	| discrepancy_id | id from discrepancies.csv (`D-0001`) |
    28	| decision | `A`, `B` or `other` |
    29	| chosen_value | the value to write when decision is `other` (required then; ignored otherwise) |
    30	| adjudicator | who decided (`sean`, or `human-<initials>` if delegated) |
    31	| date | ISO date |
    32	| reason | one sentence; for methods-paper outcome #4 use the vocabulary misread, wrong row, unit, omission, source ambiguity, other |

   148	def cmd_diff(args):
   149	    header_a, rows_a = read_csv(args.A, KEY_FIELDS, "A")
   150	    header_b, rows_b = read_csv(args.B, KEY_FIELDS, "B")

   156	    by_type = {}

   161	    for t in ["missing_in_A", "missing_in_B", "numeric", "text", "provenance"]:

   166	def validate_log(log_rows, disc):
   167	    problems = []
   168	    seen = {}
   169	    disc_by_id = {d["discrepancy_id"]: d for d in disc}
   170	    for i, r in enumerate(log_rows, start=2):
   171	        did = r["discrepancy_id"]
   172	        if did in seen:
   173	            problems.append("adjudication log line %d: %s already adjudicated on line %d" % (i, did, seen[did]))
   174	            continue
   175	        seen[did] = i
   176	        if did not in disc_by_id:
   177	            problems.append("adjudication log line %d: %s is not a discrepancy of these two files (stale or wrong log)" % (i, did))
   178	            continue
   179	        d = disc_by_id[did]
   180	        if r["decision"] not in ("A", "B", "other"):
   181	            problems.append("adjudication log line %d (%s): decision must be A, B or other, got '%s'" % (i, did, r["decision"]))
   182	        if r["decision"] == "other":
   183	            if d["field"] == ROW_FIELD:
   184	                problems.append("adjudication log line %d (%s): a whole-row discrepancy takes decision A or B, not other" % (i, did))
   185	            elif r["chosen_value"] == "":
   186	                problems.append("adjudication log line %d (%s): decision other needs a chosen_value" % (i, did))
   187	        for f in ("adjudicator", "date", "reason"):
   188	            if r[f] == "":
   189	                problems.append("adjudication log line %d (%s): %s is blank" % (i, did, f))
   190	        if r["date"]:
   191	            try:
   192	                _dt.date.fromisoformat(r["date"])
   193	            except ValueError:
   194	                problems.append("adjudication log line %d (%s): date '%s' is not ISO (YYYY-MM-DD)" % (i, did, r["date"]))
   195	    unlogged = [d for d in disc if d["discrepancy_id"] not in seen]
   196	    for d in unlogged:
   197	        problems.append("discrepancy %s has no adjudication-log row (%s; field %s; A='%s'; B='%s'; type %s)" %
   198	                        (d["discrepancy_id"], d["key"], d["field"], d["value_A"], d["value_B"], d["type"]))
   199	    if unlogged:
   200	        problems.append("refusing to build: %d of %d discrepancies are not adjudicated" % (len(unlogged), len(disc)))
   201	    return problems, {r["discrepancy_id"]: r for r in log_rows}

   204	def merge_meta(a, b, field):
   205	    """Common value, or the only value (row kept from one file), or A=<a>;B=<b> when the two runs differ."""
   206	    if a == b or b == "":
   207	        return a
   208	    if a == "":
   209	        return b
   210	    return "A=%s;B=%s" % (a, b)

   213	def cmd_build(args):
   214	    header_a, rows_a = read_csv(args.A, KEY_FIELDS, "A")
   215	    header_b, rows_b = read_csv(args.B, KEY_FIELDS, "B")
   216	    _, log_rows = read_csv(args.log, LOG_COLUMNS, "adjudication log")
   217	    disc, idx_a, idx_b, fields = compute_discrepancies(header_a, rows_a, header_b, rows_b)
   218	    problems, log = validate_log(log_rows, disc)
   219	    primary = None
   220	    if args.primary:
   221	        _, prim_rows = read_csv(args.primary, PRIMARY_COLUMNS, "primary-outcome")
   222	        primary = {}
   223	        for i, r in enumerate(prim_rows, start=2):
   224	            sa = (r["study_id"], r["ability_id"])
   225	            if sa in primary and primary[sa] != r["outcome_measure"]:
   226	                problems.append("primary-outcome file line %d: study %s x ability %s already has primary outcome '%s'; one per study x ability"
   227	                                % (i, sa[0], sa[1], primary[sa]))
   228	            primary[sa] = r["outcome_measure"]
   229	    if problems:
   230	        die(problems)
   231	
   232	    out_cols = list(header_a) + [c for c in header_b if c not in header_a]
   233	    if "is_primary_outcome" not in out_cols:
   234	        out_cols.insert(out_cols.index("n_tested") + 1 if "n_tested" in out_cols else len(out_cols), "is_primary_outcome")
   235	    disc_by_key = {}
   236	    for d in disc:
   237	        disc_by_key.setdefault(d["key"], []).append(d)
   238	    build_date = args.date or _dt.date.today().isoformat()
   239	    try:
   240	        _dt.date.fromisoformat(build_date)
   241	    except ValueError:
   242	        die("--date '%s' is not ISO (YYYY-MM-DD)" % build_date)
   243	
   244	    result = []
   245	    dropped = 0
   246	    for k in sorted(set(idx_a) | set(idx_b)):
   247	        ra, rb = idx_a.get(k), idx_b.get(k)
   248	        dlist = disc_by_key.get(k, [])
   249	        row_d = [d for d in dlist if d["field"] == ROW_FIELD]
   250	        if row_d:
   251	            dec = log[row_d[0]["discrepancy_id"]]["decision"]
   252	            src = ra if ra is not None else rb
   253	            present_in = "A" if ra is not None else "B"
   254	            if dec != present_in:  # adjudicator chose the file where the row is absent: drop it
   255	                dropped += 1
   256	                continue
   257	            new = {c: src.get(c, "") for c in out_cols}
   258	            meta_a = ra if ra is not None else {}
   259	            meta_b = rb if rb is not None else {}
   260	        else:
   261	            new = {}
   262	            for c in out_cols:
   263	                if c in KEY_FIELDS or c in RUN_METADATA_FIELDS:
   264	                    new[c] = ra.get(c, "") if c in KEY_FIELDS else ""
   265	                else:
   266	                    new[c] = ra.get(c, "") if ra.get(c, "") == rb.get(c, "") else None
   267	            for d in dlist:
   268	                entry = log[d["discrepancy_id"]]
   269	                if entry["decision"] == "A":
   270	                    new[d["field"]] = ra.get(d["field"], "")
   271	                elif entry["decision"] == "B":
   272	                    new[d["field"]] = rb.get(d["field"], "")
   273	                else:
   274	                    new[d["field"]] = entry["chosen_value"]
   275	            for c in out_cols:
   276	                if new[c] is None:  # equivalent but not identical numerics (e.g. 1 vs 1.0): keep A's printed form
   277	                    new[c] = ra.get(c, "")
   278	            meta_a, meta_b = ra, rb
   279	        new["extractor_id"] = "reconciled"
   280	        new["extraction_date"] = build_date
   281	        new["skill_version"] = merge_meta(meta_a.get("skill_version", ""), meta_b.get("skill_version", ""), "skill_version")
   282	        new["model"] = merge_meta(meta_a.get("model", ""), meta_b.get("model", ""), "model")
   283	        result.append(new)
   284	
   285	    # is_primary_outcome
   286	    if primary is None:
   287	        for r in result:
   288	            r["is_primary_outcome"] = ""
   289	        warn("no --primary file given: is_primary_outcome left blank on every row; nothing will enter pooling until it is set")
   290	    else:
   291	        matched = set()
   292	        for r in result:
   293	            sa = (r["study_id"], r["ability_id"])
   294	            if sa in primary and primary[sa] == r["outcome_measure"]:
   295	                r["is_primary_outcome"] = "yes"
   296	                matched.add(sa)
   297	            else:
   298	                r["is_primary_outcome"] = "no"
   299	        for sa in sorted({(r["study_id"], r["ability_id"]) for r in result} - matched):
   300	            warn("study %s x ability %s has no is_primary_outcome = yes row (no matching primary-outcome entry)" % sa)
   301	        for sa in sorted(set(primary) - matched):
   302	            warn("primary-outcome entry %s x %s ('%s') matches no reconciled row" % (sa[0], sa[1], primary[sa]))
   303	
   304	    write_csv(args.out, out_cols, result)
   305	    print("reconcile build: %d discrepancies applied from %s; %d row(s) written, %d row(s) dropped by adjudication -> %s" %
   306	          (len(disc), args.log, len(result), dropped, args.out))
   307	    return 0
   308

   310	def main(argv=None):
   311	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Diff two extractor files and build the reconciled master (tools/RECONCILIATION.md)")
   312	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
   313	    d = sub.add_parser("diff", help="list every field-level discrepancy between A and B")
   314	    d.add_argument("A"); d.add_argument("B"); d.add_argument("--out", required=True)
   315	    d.set_defaults(func=cmd_diff)
   316	    b = sub.add_parser("build", help="apply the adjudication log and write master_reconciled.csv")
   317	    b.add_argument("A"); b.add_argument("B"); b.add_argument("log"); b.add_argument("--out", required=True)
   318	    b.add_argument("--primary", help="CSV with study_id, ability_id, outcome_measure naming the primary outcome per study x ability")
   319	    b.add_argument("--date", help="extraction_date written on reconciled rows (default: today, ISO)")
   320	    b.set_defaults(func=cmd_build)
   321	    args = p.parse_args(argv)
   322	    return args.func(args)
   323	
   324	
   325	if __name__ == "__main__":
   326	    sys.exit(main())

=== research-project.md 44-56
**Population baselines.** The SDs below are between-person values in healthy adults; each strength score divides by one of them.

| Variable | Mean ± SD | Source and sample |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resting heart rate | 65.5 ± 7.7 bpm | Quer et al. 2020 \[86\]; 92,457 adults, wearable, all monitored days |
| Systolic blood pressure | 122 mmHg; SD ≈ 17 (derived: 15.6 from the interquartile range 110 to 131, 17.9 from the 5th to 95th percentile span 98 to 157) | Wright et al. 2011 \[87\]; NHANES 2001 to 2008, adults 18+ |
| Axillary (core) temperature | 35.97 ± 0.48 °C | Geneva et al. 2019 \[88\]; 551 measurements, 5 studies |
| Left to right hand skin-temperature difference | 0.31 ± 0.25 °C | Uematsu et al. 1988 \[89\]; n = 56, hand dorsum |
| Fingertip skin temperature at 23 °C room | 27.16 ± 3.2 °C | Gatt et al. 2019 \[90\]; 51 healthy controls, 510 finger readings |
| Pupil diameter, photopic (16 lux) | 4.03 ± 0.9 mm | Schröder et al. 2018 \[91\]; 91 normal eyes |
| Hearing threshold at 250 Hz | SD ≈ 5 dB (model estimate about 4 dB) | Shahnaz & Ciocca 2026 \[92\]; 126 young adults with typical hearing |

Two studies report their own baselines, which the notes carry: Kozhevnikov's practitioners started at 36.49 °C (SD 0.21) \[4\], and Eberhardt's subject had a 4.96 mm pupil at trial onset \[39\]. Scores use the population SD throughout so that abilities stay comparable; dividing the 2.2 °C core rise by the within-study SD would give 10.5 instead of 4.6.
=== research-project.md line 17
**Scope.** An ability is included when a person initiates the change in their own body and the change was measured objectively or by a validated rating. Indirect levers count (paced breathing, skeletal-muscle tension, imagery, hypnotic suggestion, instrument feedback), because the lever is itself part of the finding. Three things are excluded from scoring and handled descriptively: effects the person does not initiate (placebo analgesia given by others, classically conditioned immune responses); links that run through implanted or external hardware to a machine or another person; and clinical benefit as such, since the certainty rating asks only whether the control exists.

    aid,name,syn,eid,ks=cells

EOF
